evidence: For P_n, each maximal uncertain run of length r is a path P_r whose edges must cover it; definite vertices have no incident disagreement edges. The parity constraint on consecutive definite bits is equality for no gap, impossible for a run of length one, opposite bits for a gap of length two (one mandatory edge), equal bits for a gap of length three (two mandatory edges), and free for length at least four (take all edges or omit one interior edge, giving both parities). The consecutive constraints are equivalent to the anchor constraints by parity additivity. At either boundary, or for an all-uncertain word, the run has no parity constraint and is allowed exactly for r≥2, with r=0 representing absence.

Put Q=1+t²/(1−t) for the boundary/all-uncertain contribution and G=1+t²+t³+2t⁴/(1−t) for a gap between consecutive definite bits including multiplicities. A word is all uncertain, or has Q on both ends, two choices of first definite bit and a sequence of gap/new-definite-bit steps. Thus its length series is Q+2tQ²/(1−tG)=(1+t+t³+t⁴)/(1−t−t²−t³).
